key_insight: The first U.S. CADASIL cohort shows that a standardized, multicenter natural-history framework can capture early clinical, functional, imaging, and biomarker differences in a monogenic small-vessel disease model of VCID.
clinical_relevance: These baseline data may help improve patient stratification, biomarker development, and trial readiness for CADASIL and related vascular cognitive impairment studies.
method: Cross-sectional baseline analysis from 12 U.S. enrollment sites (Oct 2022–Jan 2025)
Compared CADASIL NOTCH3 carriers with non-carrier family controls using standardized clinical, cognitive, physical, MRI, genetic, and proteomic assessments
Used centralized variant classification and multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, race, and education
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 560 baseline participants, with an analytic cohort of 343 CADASIL carriers and 116 controls, enabling group comparisons across multimodal measures.
watch_item: The findings are baseline, cross-sectional observations from a highly selected family-based cohort, so they may not generalize to all patients or predict individual outcomes.
paper_title: The United States CADASIL Consortium: Baseline Findings from a Natural History Study
